q: The sea water contains many salts such as ____, potassium chloride, magnesium sulphate, magnesium chloride and magnesium bromide.
e: Sodium chloride is the most abundant salt dissolved in seawater.

q: The Earth's crust is made up of minerals containing various types of salts such as calcium fluoride (fluorite), magnesium sulphate (____), lead(II) sulphide (galena) and calcium carbonate (limestone), etc.
e: Magnesium sulphate is commonly known as Epsom salt.

q: The Earth's crust is made up of minerals containing various types of salts such as calcium fluoride (fluorite), magnesium sulphate (Epsom salt), lead(II) sulphide (galena) and calcium carbonate (____), etc.
e: Calcium carbonate is the primary component of limestone.

q: A salt is produced when an acid reacts with a ____.
e: The neutralization reaction between an acid and a base yields a salt.

q: The salt consists of two parts. One part comes from the base, the other from the ____.
e: The positive ion of a salt typically comes from the base, and the negative ion from the acid.

q: The sodium ion ($Na^+$) part of the salt comes from the base and the chloride ion ($Cl^-$) comes from the ____.
e: In sodium chloride, the chloride ion is derived from hydrochloric acid.

q: When an acid reacts with a base, a salt and water are formed. This reaction is known as ____.
e: Neutralization is the specific term for the reaction between an acid and a base.

q: It involves the combination of $H^+$ ion produced from acid and $OH^-$ ion produced from base to form ____.
e: The hydrogen and hydroxide ions combine to form water molecules during neutralization.

q: Neutralisation reaction occurs in our stomach. The acid (HCl) produced by our stomach, is so strong that it is ____ with a base produced by cells.
e: The stomach lining secretes bases to protect itself from its own strong acid.

q: Salts are also produced when an acid reacts with a metal or a metal ____.
e: Acids react with both reactive metals and metal carbonates to produce salts.

q: hydrochloric acid HCl produces ____ salts.
e: The anion in hydrochloric acid forms chloride salts.

q: sulphuric acid $H_2SO_4$ produces ____ salts.
e: The anion in sulphuric acid forms sulphate salts.

q: nitric acid $HNO_3$ produces ____ salts.
e: The anion in nitric acid forms nitrate salts.

q: sulphurous acid $H_2SO_3$ produces ____ salts.
e: The anion in sulphurous acid forms sulphite salts.

q: carbonic acid $H_2CO_3$ produces ____ salts.
e: The anion in carbonic acid forms carbonate salts.

q: ethanoic acid $CH_3COOH$ produces ____ salt.
e: The anion in ethanoic acid forms ethanoate salts.

q: all ____ are soluble.
e: There are no common insoluble nitrate salts.

q: all chlorides are soluble except silver, mercury(I), ____.
e: Lead(II) chloride is a notable exception to the general solubility of chlorides.

q: all sulphates are soluble except ____, lead(II), calcium.
e: Barium sulphate is highly insoluble and used in medical imaging.

q: carbonates of sodium, potassium and ____ are soluble.
e: Most carbonates are insoluble, except those of sodium, potassium, and ammonium.

q: The preparation method depends on whether the salt is ____ in water or not.
e: Solubility dictates whether crystallization or precipitation is used to prepare the salt.

q: Soluble salts are usually prepared by ____ method.
e: Evaporating the water from a soluble salt solution yields crystals.

q: Insoluble salts are usually prepared by ____ method.
e: Mixing two soluble solutions causes an insoluble salt to precipitate out.

q: Salts of sodium, potassium and ammonium can be prepared from caustic soda solution (NaOH), caustic potash solution (KOH) and ammonia solution ($NH_4OH$), respectively, by the ____ using the appropriate acid.
e: Titration and neutralization are used to prepare salts of highly reactive metals.

q: Insoluble salts are prepared by ____.
e: Precipitation reactions occur when two soluble salts react to form an insoluble product.

q: A ____ precipitate of barium sulphate, $BaSO_4$, is formed.
e: Barium sulphate forms a distinct white solid during precipitation.

q: sodium chloride NaCl is used as a food ____.
e: Sodium chloride is common table salt, used to flavor and preserve food.

q: sodium sulphate $Na_2SO_4$, sodium nitrite $NaNO_2$, sodium citrate $Na_3C_6H_5O_7$ are used as food ____.
e: These salts help prevent spoilage and extend the shelf life of food.

q: ammonium sulphate $(NH_4)_2SO_4$, ammonium nitrate $NH_4NO_3$, ammonium phosphate $(NH_4)_3PO_4$ are used as ____.
e: These ammonium salts provide essential nitrogen and phosphorus to plants.

q: potassium chloride KCl is used as a ____.
e: Potassium chloride supplies potassium, a vital macronutrient for crops.

q: magnesium sulphate $MgSO_4 \cdot 7H_2O$ is used for medical uses (____).
e: Epsom salt is commonly used in baths to soothe muscles.

q: magnesium hydroxide $Mg(OH)_2$ is used for medical uses (____, MOM).
e: Milk of magnesia is an antacid and laxative.

q: calcium sulphate $CaSO_4$ is used for medical uses (____, POP).
e: Plaster of Paris is used to make casts for broken bones.

q: A salt is a substance produced from the reaction between an acid and a base or a ____.
e: Reactive metals can displace hydrogen from acids to form salts.

q: Based on the ____, salts can be classified as chlorides, sulphates, nitrates, sulphites and carbonates, etc.
e: The negative ion in a salt determines its classification and comes from the parent acid.

q: Soluble salts are usually prepared from the reactions between metals and dilute acids followed by ____.
e: The resulting solution is evaporated to crystallize the soluble salt.

q: Insoluble salts are usually prepared by ____ method.
e: Precipitation is the standard method for isolating insoluble salts.

q: Neutralisation is the reaction between an acid and a base to form a salt and ____ only.
e: Water and a salt are the exclusive products of a true neutralization reaction.
